title: Mechanisms and Adaptations of Mammalian Hibernation
context:
A. Hibernation represents an extreme physiological adaptation characterised by profound metabolic suppression and regulated hypothermia. In 2012, Dr Elena Rostova at the Fairbanks Institute of Arctic Biology conducted investigations into the Arctic ground squirrel (Urocitellus parryii). During deep torpor in Alaska, this rodent reduces its basal metabolic rate to 2 percent of resting levels. Astonishingly, its core body temperature plunges to minus 2.9 degrees Celsius without freezing, a phenomenon known as supercooling. This state is sustained because the animal systematically eliminates endogenous ice-nucleating agents from its bloodstream, preventing crystallisation within vascular tissues.

B. At the cellular level, the entry into torpor requires precise biochemical switches. Research directed by Dr Marcus Vance in 2015 at the University of Tromsø demonstrated that the activation of central A1 adenosine receptors initiates hypometabolism. When these receptors are stimulated, mitochondrial respiration decreases, mediated by phosphorylation of electron transport chain complexes. Furthermore, global protein synthesis falls by more than 90 percent to conserve energy. Concurrently, an intracellular enzyme called AMP-activated protein kinase reorganises metabolic flux, diverting resources from carbohydrate catabolism toward the oxidation of stored lipid reserves held within white adipose depots.

C. The cardiovascular adjustments demanded by hibernation are equally striking. In non-hibernating mammals, severe hypothermia precipitates ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest. However, hibernators possess specialized electrophysiological safeguards. In 2017, the Zurich Cardiovascular Laboratory examined European hedgehogs (Erinaceus europaeus) and recorded heart rates dropping from 350 beats per minute to roughly 4 beats per minute. This extreme bradycardia is tolerated because specialised calcium-handling proteins, predominantly an altered isoform of SERCA2a, maintain ion equilibrium. Concurrently, modified cardiac titin filaments provide myocardial flexibility, allowing ventricular pumping against heightened blood viscosity.

D. Prolonged inactivity in humans induces muscular atrophy and skeletal decalcification. Yet, hibernating black bears (Ursus americanus) in Minnesota, studied by Dr Hannah Lindqvist in 2019, remain dormant for up to seven months without structural degradation. Lindqvist revealed that skeletal integrity is sustained by parathyroid hormone-related protein, which suppresses osteoclast activity while maintaining osteoblastic bone deposition. Additionally, bears do not urinate during winter sleep; instead, gut microbiota hydrolyse circulating urea into ammonia, which hepatic pathways recycle into new amino acids, thereby preserving skeletal muscle mass.

E. Deep torpor is periodically punctuated by brief intervals termed interbout arousals. Every 10 to 20 days, animals generate heat via brown adipose tissue, elevating body temperature to 37 degrees Celsius for approximately 12 hours. At the Kyoto Bioscience Institute in 2021, Professor Kenji Sato discovered that during torpor, cortical neurons lose substantial numbers of dendritic spines. Remarkably, these neural connections reassemble within two hours of arousal. Sato also observed elevated phosphorylated tau protein—a pathological hallmark of Alzheimer's disease—which dissolves completely upon rewarming, leaving no neurological deficits.

F. The discovery of primate hibernation opened new possibilities for translational medicine. In 2023, Dr Sophie Girard examined the fat-tailed dwarf lemur (Cheirogaleus medius) in the Kirindy Forest of western Madagascar. Girard confirmed that this tropical primate can hibernate in tree hollows for seven months despite ambient temperatures reaching 30 degrees Celsius. These findings have spurred efforts to induce synthetic torpor in humans. Space agencies project that synthetic torpor could reduce consumable demands during crewed missions to Mars in the late 2030s, while clinical trials explore its potential to limit tissue necrosis after ischaemic stroke.

questions.prompt: Who investigated the Arctic ground squirrel at the Fairbanks Institute of Arctic Biology in 2012?

questions.prompt: To what percentage of resting levels does the Arctic ground squirrel reduce its basal metabolic rate?

questions.prompt: To what temperature in degrees Celsius can the Arctic ground squirrel's core body plunge without freezing?

questions.quote: plunges to minus 2.9 degrees Celsius without freezing, a phenomenon known as supercooling.

questions.prompt: What term refers to the process of remaining unfrozen below freezing temperatures?
questions.why: Đoạn A định nghĩa hiện tượng nhiệt độ cơ thể xuống dưới điểm đông nhưng không đóng băng là 'supercooling' (hiện tượng quá lạnh).
questions.quote: plunges to minus 2.9 degrees Celsius without freezing, a phenomenon known as supercooling.

questions.prompt: What agents does the Arctic ground squirrel eliminate from its blood to prevent freezing?
questions.why: Đoạn A giải thích rằng loài vật này chủ động đào thải các tác nhân tạo mầm đá ('endogenous ice-nucleating agents') khỏi máu.
questions.quote: systematically eliminates endogenous ice-nucleating agents from its bloodstream, preventing crystallisation within vascular tissues.

questions.prompt: Who directed research on the cellular triggers of torpor at the University of Tromsø in 2015?
questions.why: Đoạn B nêu rõ nghiên cứu về các cơ chế kích hoạt sinh hóa ở cấp độ tế bào năm 2015 được chỉ đạo bởi Dr Marcus Vance.
questions.quote: Research directed by Dr Marcus Vance in 2015 at the University of Tromsø demonstrated

questions.quote: activation of central A1 adenosine receptors initiates hypometabolism.

questions.prompt: By more than what percentage does protein synthesis fall during torpor?
questions.why: Đoạn B ghi nhận quá trình tổng hợp protein nói chung giảm hơn 90 phần trăm ('90 percent') nhằm tiết kiệm năng lượng.
questions.quote: protein synthesis falls by more than 90 percent to conserve energy.

questions.prompt: What enzyme redirects metabolic resources toward the oxidation of stored fat?
questions.why: Đoạn B nêu tên loại enzyme nội bào có tên là AMP-activated protein kinase chịu trách nhiệm tái tổ chức luồng trao đổi chất sang đốt cháy mỡ.
questions.quote: an intracellular enzyme called AMP-activated protein kinase reorganises metabolic flux, diverting resources from carbohydrate catabolism toward the oxidation of stored lipid reserves

questions.prompt: Which institution investigated the cardiac responses of European hedgehogs in 2017?
questions.why: Đoạn C xác nhận đơn vị nghiên cứu tiến hành kiểm tra trên loài nhím châu Âu vào năm 2017 là Zurich Cardiovascular Laboratory.

questions.prompt: What protein preserves bone integrity in dormant black bears?
